message.content: **Summary:** I reviewed the saved notes (long-term holder, large-cap tech preference, dividends reinvested manually) and the account ($50,000 cash, 100 shares of MSFT, no AAPL position), then checked AAPL's quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and pulled the FY2024 10-K figures filed 2024-11-01: revenue of $391,035M, net income of $93,736M, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — a business profile consistent with the mandate's large-cap technology preference and with a long-term holding horizon. I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at $222.80, a limit just above the ask so it would execute near market; it filled at $222.80 for a total of $9,803.20, which stays under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap, uses only existing cash (no money moved out of the account), and complies with the AAPL/MSFT-only, buy-only restrictions. No MSFT order was placed, leaving $10,196.80 of today's allowance unused if a further qualifying opportunity arises.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 222.80, 44 shares = $9,803.20. Under $10,000 per order, total today $9,803.20 < $20,000. Cash was $50,000, no money moved out.
